svg.title: One Corporate Buyer Cohort, Five Nested Stages
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-corporate-buyer-cohort; chart type: funnel; title: One Corporate Buyer Cohort, Five Nested Stages; subtitle: Measure collected and settled business rather than proposal volume.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative cohort of 200 distinct corporate prospects followed through their events and final settlement, not necessarily within 30 days. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Counts are neither ticket quantities nor canonical revenue inputs.; caption: Conditional conversion is 50%, 50%, 40%, then 60%; 12 settled accounts represent 6% of the original cohort.; stages: label: Screened corporate prospects; value: 200 distinct prospect accounts; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Identify a named buyer, relevant event, plausible group size, and legitimate business contact route. Deduplicate accounts before counting outreach across multiple employees.; label: Qualified event buyers; value: 100 accounts; 50% of prospects; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Confirm spending authority, event dates, seat requirements, payment method, and procurement timing. Exclude accounts whose collection timetable cannot fund supplier commitments.; label: Executable package offers; value: 50 accounts; 50% of qualified buyers; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Issue inventory-backed offers with expiration times, mandatory charges, precise inclusions, transfer conditions, and cancellation terms. A speculative supplier inquiry does not qualify as an executable offer.; label: Collected buyer deposits; value: 20 accounts; 40% of offers; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Count cleared deposits tied to accepted contracts, not unsigned purchase orders. Record deposits as liabilities until performance supports revenue recognition; retain liquidity against refundable amounts.; label: Fulfilled settled accounts; value: 12 accounts; 60% of depositors; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Require completed delivery, reconciled supplier costs, cleared final payment, and documented residual exposure. The other eight depositors remain pending or are canceled; their deposits are not automatically earned profit.

text.title: One Corporate Buyer Cohort, Five Nested Stages
text.tspan: One Corporate Buyer Cohort, Five Nested Stages

rect.title: label: Screened corporate prospects; value: 200 distinct prospect accounts; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Identify a named buyer, relevant event, plausible group size, and legitimate business contact route. Deduplicate accounts before counting outreach across multiple employees.

label: Qualified event buyers; value: 100 accounts; 50% of prospects; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Confirm spending authority, event dates, seat requirements, payment method, and procurement timing. Exclude accounts whose collection timetable cannot fund supplier commitments.

label: Executable package offers; value: 50 accounts; 50% of qualified buyers; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Issue inventory-backed offers with expiration times, mandatory charges, precise inclusions, transfer conditions, and cancellation terms. A speculative supplier inquiry does not qualify as an executable offer.

label: Collected buyer deposits; value: 20 accounts; 40% of offers; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Count cleared deposits tied to accepted contracts, not unsigned purchase orders. Record deposits as liabilities until performance supports revenue recognition; retain liquidity against refundable amounts.

label: Fulfilled settled accounts; value: 12 accounts; 60% of depositors; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Require completed delivery, reconciled supplier costs, cleared final payment, and documented residual exposure. The other eight depositors remain pending or are canceled; their deposits are not automatically earned profit.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative cohort of 200 distinct corporate prospects followed through their events and final settlement, not necessarily within 30 days. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Counts are neither ticket quantities nor canonical revenue inputs.
